note: Interrogative 'why' should be لِمَ or لماذا; current unmarked لم is confusable with negation.
proposed_english: Why did you buy this car?

note: Interrogative 'why' should be لِمَ or لماذا.
proposed_english: Why did you disobey my order?

note: Interrogative 'why' should be لِمَ or لماذا.
proposed_english: Why did you quit your job?

note: Current لم لم is malformed/ambiguous for learner-facing MSA; use لماذا لم.
proposed_english: Why didn't you call me earlier?

note: Current لم لن is malformed; use لماذا لن.
proposed_english: Why won't you be here tomorrow?

note: رجاءًا is misspelled (رجاءً), and المجيء إلى هنا lacks the English sense of 'come in'.
proposed_target: هل يمكنك الدخول إلى هنا، رجاءً؟
proposed_english: Could you come in here, please?

note: Standard orthography requires أن أفعلها من أجلك.
proposed_english: I can do it for you.

note: المدرس means teacher, not school; أحضر is also unsuitable here for routine travel.
proposed_english: I come to school by bus.

note: Declarative sentence incorrectly ends in a question mark.
proposed_english: I don't know what I'll do.

note: Standard orthography requires أعرف.
proposed_target: أنا لا أعرف ما يحصل هنا.
proposed_english: I don't know what happens here.

note: Arabic says 'I did not understand your meaning'; English says present 'I don't know what you mean'.
proposed_english: I don't know what you mean.

note: بالباص is colloquial/loan-register; use standard MSA بالحافلة.
proposed_english: I go to school by bus.

note: Missing initial hamza in أعتقد.
proposed_english: I guess we can't say no.

note: لا أملك المال does not express the English 'with me'.
proposed_english: I have no money with me.

note: Arabic means 'I want to tell you something'; English says 'I have something to tell you'.
proposed_target: لدي شيء أريد أن أخبرك به.
proposed_english: I have something to tell you.

note: أنك ليس معجبًا بي is ungrammatical; the intended meaning is directly expressed with لا تحبني.
proposed_english: I know you don't like me.

note: Arabic says 'I want you to trust me', not 'I need you to trust me'.
proposed_english: I want you to trust me.

note: Imperative is written افعل with hamzat al-wasl, not إفعل.
proposed_target: من فضلك افعل ما تراه ضروريًا.
proposed_english: Please do what you consider necessary.

note: For polished standard MSA, use حدّثني rather than the current form احكي in this learner sentence.
proposed_english: Please tell me about your trip.

note: ما أحتاج is incomplete/less standard here; use ما أحتاج إليه.
proposed_english: Tomorrow I'll buy what I need.

note: Interrogative relative should be لماذا/لِمَ, not bare لم.
proposed_english: We know why you did that.
